key_insight: Oxygen-ion transport in ceria-based rare-earth high-entropy oxides is controlled by a balance between vacancy availability and the local cation hopping environment, with moderate vacancy levels and Ce-rich pathways giving the best diffusion.
engineering_relevance: This identifies composition and defect-structure levers for designing solid-state electrolytes with higher oxygen-ion conductivity in chemically complex ceramics.
method: CHGNet-driven molecular dynamics simulations of Ce_x(YLaPrSm)_{1-x}O_{2-δ}
Benchmarked three CHGNet variants against targeted DFT data including f-valence electrons
Compared fluorite and bixbyite structures across temperature, Ce content, and vacancy concentration
evidence_signal: The study combines ML-potential MD with DFT benchmarking and event-level hopping analysis to link composition, structure, and diffusion trends across multiple RE-HEO conditions.
watch_item: Predictions depend on the quality of the CHGNet potential and its transferability to lanthanide-rich chemistries, so additional validation is important before deployment.
paper_title: Ionic Diffusion Properties of Rare-Earth High-Entropy Oxides from a Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential
